title: Softmax in one pass
prompt: Fold scores into a softmax one at a time, keeping two numbers: the largest score so far, m (starting at minus infinity), and l, the sum of exp(s - m) over the scores so far (starting at 0). Write online(scores) returning (m, l). When a score raises the max, the old sum was relative to the old max: rescale it.
starter:
import math

def online(scores: list[float]) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """the running max m and sum l of exp(s - m), in one pass over the scores"""
    m, l = -math.inf, 0.0
    for s in scores:
        m = max(m, s)
        l = l + math.exp(s - m)
    return m, l
hints: Keep the old max before updating it: m_new = max(m, s).
Rescale the old sum by exp(m - m_new), then add exp(s - m_new).
At the start m is minus infinity and l is 0, and exp(-inf) is 0, so the first score needs no special case.
explain: When a bigger score arrives, every term already in l was computed against the old max. Multiplying by exp(m_old - m_new) converts them all at once: exp(s - m_old)·exp(m_old - m_new) = exp(s - m_new). So one pass gives the same (m, l) as computing the max first and the sum second, up to rounding. That's what lets flash attention stream keys through shared memory and never store a whole row of scores. The starter forgets the rescale, so it's only right while the max never changes, as in [3, 2, 1].
